JUDGMENT
This petition under Section 166 MV act is filed seeking compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by the Petitioner in a road traffic accident.

2. It is stated that on 07-01-2023 at about 7.10 p.m., the Petitioner was proceeding on his motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-40-K-7331 from his village Muddenhalli towards Chikkaballapura Town along with his relatives Akshay and Muniyappa as a pillion riders and when they reached near Anjaneyaswamy Temple, Nandi-Chikkaballapura Road, Chikkaballapura Town, Chikkaballapura District, at that time, the driver of the Maruthi Brezza Car bearing Reg. No.KA-40-N-1609 (hereinafter called as offending vehicle) came with high speed and in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner's motorcycle.
Due to the accident, the petitioner has fell down on the road along with motorcycle and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately after the accident the petitioner taken to Govt. Hospital, Chikkaballapura, wherein he has taken first aid treatment and thereafter he was shifted to Nimhans hospital and thereafter he was shifted Digvijay Hospital,
Bengaluru, wherein he has taken treatment as an inpatient from 08-01-2023 to 10-01-2023 and again he was shifted to Victoria Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein he has taken treatment as an inpatient from 11-01-2023 to 19-01-2023.
Due to the accidental injuries, he is suffering from permanent disability and unable to lead normal life as earlier.
It is claimed that Petitioner has spent Rs.2,00,000/- for treatment, medicines, conveyance and other charges.

At the time of accident,
Petitioner was aged 28 years, working as a Carpenter under different employers and earning a sum of Rs.20,000/- per month.
Due to accidental injuries he has lost his earning capacity and income.
As the accident was caused due to negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle, it is requested to award compensation from the Respondent No.1- Insured and Respondent No.2- insurer.
3. In response to the petition notice, the Respondent No.1 and 2 have appeared before the court through their counsel and filed their written statement.
4. The Respondent No.1 has filed his written statement and contended that the petition filed by the petitioner is not maintainable either in law or on facts.
He has denied the age, occupation, income of the Petitioner, and the future expenses claimed by him, expenses incurred by him and disability suffered by him.

He has admitted that he is the RC owner of offending vehicle and the same was insured with the respondent No.2 and the same was valid from 31-08- 2022 to 30-08-2023 and the driver of the car was having valid and effective driving licence to drive the vehicle as on the date of accident.

Further contended that, the accident has not occurred due to negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle, on the other hand, the accident has occurred due to sole negligence on the part of the rider of the petitioner and has prayed for dismissal of the petition.
5.
The Respondent No.2 has filed its written statement and denied the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.
Further, denied the contents of petition averments in toto.
The concerned police and owner of the offending vehicle have not complied the mandatory provision of Section 159 and 134 (c) of M.V.Act.

This respondent has admitted the issuance of policy in respect of offending vehicle, its validity as on the date of the accident but its liability if any is subject to terms Shashikumar M.K vs Vedamurthy on 10 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/14556699/
2 and conditions of the policy.

Further contended that, the accident has not occurred due to negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle, on the other hand, the accident has occurred due to sole negligence on the part of the rider of the motorcycle as the petitioner was proceeding along with two pillion riders.

Further contended that the driver of the offending vehicle was not having DL and was not holding valid and effective driving licence as on the date of accident and the driver has violated the policy terms and conditions.

Respondent No.2 further has disputed that the nature of injuries sustained by the Petitioner, avocation and income of the Petitioner, and the future expenses claimed by him, expenses incurred by him and disability suffered by him and has prayed for dismissal of the petition.

6. On the basis of the above pleadings, the following recasted Issues were framed :-
1.

Whether the Petitioner proves that pm 07-01-2023 at about 7.10 p.m. near Anjaneyaswamy temple, Nandi- Chikkaballapura road, Chikkaballapura, he sustained injuries, he sustained injuries in a road traffic accident due to rash or negligent driving of the driver of the Car bearing No.Ka-40-N-1609?
2. Whether the respondent No.1 proves that the offending vehicle is validly insured with respondent No.2 and respondent No.1 is not liable to pay any compensation?
3. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as claimed, If so from whom and to what extent?
4. What order or award?
Additional Issue 1. Whether the respondent No.2 proves that the policy conditions are violated by respondent No.1 and the respondent No.2 is not liable to pay any compensation?
7.

In order to prove the claim, the Petitioner examined himself as PW.1 and in support of his case, 2 witnesses are examined as PW-2 and 3 and got marked the documents as per Ex.P.1 to P.22 respectively.

8. By considering the available materials on record and the arguments addressed by the parties, I have answered the above Issues as under:
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative.
Issue No.2: Does not survive for consideration.
Issue No 3 : In the partly Affirmative Additional issue: In the negative.
Issue No.4: As per the final order, for the following:

3 9. ISSUE NO.1:- The case of the petitioner is that on 07-01-2023 at about 7.10 p.m., he was riding his motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-40-K-7331 from his village Muddenhalli towards Chikkaballapura Town along with his relatives Akshay and Muniyappa as a pillion riders and when they reached near Anjaneyaswamy Temple, Nandi-Chikkaballapura Road, Chikkaballapura Town,
Chikkaballapura District, at that time, the driver of the Maruthi Brezza Car bearing Reg.
No.KA-40-N-1609 came with high speed and in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner's motorcycle and caused the accident.
Due to the accident, the petitioners have fell down on the road along with motorcycle and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately after the accident the petitioner was shifted to Govt. Hospital, Chikkaballapura, wherein he has taken first aid treatment and thereafter he was shifted to Nimhans hospital and thereafter he was shifted Digvijay Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein he has taken treatment as an inpatient from 08-01-2023 to 10-01-2023 and again he was shifted to Victoria Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein he has taken treatment as an inpatient from 11-01-2023 to 10-01-2023.
10. In order to substantiate his case, petitioner has examined as PW-1 and got marked the documents at Ex.P.1 to 17.

To support of his claim, Medical Record Officer at Victoria Hospital,
Bengaluru, by name Nagaraja. G.V., was examined as PW-2 and he has produced the 3 documents at Ex.P.18 to 20.

Further, Dr. R. Kantharaju was examined as PW-3 and he has produced the 2 documents at Ex.P.21 and 22.
11.

Responded No.2-insurance company has contended that the accident has occurred due to sole negligence on the part of the rider of the motorcycle as the petitioner was proceeding along with two pillion riders.
and there was no negligence of driver of the offending vehicle.
12. During the course of cross examination of PW1, the learned counsel for the Respondent no 2 and 4 have put forth above said suggestion, however PW-1 has denied the said suggestions.
Except the suggestions, there are no documents to show that it was the negligence of the petitioner.
PW1 has stated that car dashed to motorcycle in such as high speed they all three jumped for the motorcycle and fell on the road.
The said fact neither denied by the Respondent no.2 by way putting suggestion nor putting any questions.
13. On perusal of police and medical records, it appears that the petitioner sustained injuries in a RTA.
The police records show that due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle the accident was caused.
As a result, the petitioner sustained grievous injuries.
There is no materials to disbelieve or rebut the evidence of the petitioner and charge sheet has been filed against the offending vehicle.
Absolutely there are no materials to overcome the charge sheet findings.

Therefore, this tribunal concludes that the accident occurred due to the negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle and thereby the accident was caused and petitioner has sustained injuries in a RTA.
Hence, Issue No.1 is answered in the Affirmative.
14. ISSUE NO.2:- Since the respondent No.2 has admited that policy was in force as on the date of alleged accident.
Therefore, this issue does not survive for consideration.

Shashikumar M.K vs Vedamurthy on 10 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/14556699/
4 15.
ADDITIONAL ISSUE:
The respondent No.2 has taken a contention that the owner of the offending vehicle has violated the terms and condition incorporated in the policy.

Therefore, the respondent No.2 is not liable to pay any compensation to the petitioner and respondent No.2-insurance company is absolved from its liability to reimburse the owner of the offending vehicle.
The onus of proof will be on the person who wants to rebut the presumption.
The Respondent No.2 not choose to lead positive evidence that its company is absolved from its liability to reimburse the owner of the offending vehicle.
Whatever, the contention raised by the Respondent No.2 in his written statement remains as pleading only.
They have not proved by the Respondent no.2.
It is settled principle of law that the allegation of the fact can be proved by providing evidence or by eliciting something from the mouth of the opponent.
Keeping in view of modes of proving an allegation of fact, again say that the Respondent no.2 has failed to prove his contention.

Therefore,
the respondent No.2 is liable to pay any compensation to the petitioner.
Hence I answer additional issue in the negative.
16. ISSUE NO.3:-

As per Ex.P.6 wound certificate, the petitioner has sustained the following injuries:
1. Wedge and central compression fracture of D6 Vertebral body.
2. Fracture of spinous processes of C7, D4 to D6.
3. Fracture of 1st and 2nd rib and left side hydropneumothorax
The doctor opined that the above injuries are grievous in nature.
17. Due to the accident the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately he was taken to Government Hospital, Chikkaballapura, Wherein, he was treated as an outpatient and on the same date he was referred to Nimhans Hospital, wherein he was treated as an outpatient and thereafter he was admitted in Digvijay Hospital from 08-01-2023 to 10- 01-2023 and again he was shifted to Victoria Hospital, wherein he has taken treatment as an inpatient from 11-01-2023 to 19-01-2023.

He has stated that at the time of accident, he was a Carpenter and earning a sum of Rs.20,000/-
p.m.
Due to the accidental injuries he has suffered loss of income.
He has lost his normal life as earlier and suffering huge loss of income.

18. The Petitioner has examined Medical record technician at Victoria hospital, Bengaluru as PW-2 and he has produced Authorization letter, MLC register extract and case sheet at Ex.P.18 to 20.
19.

PW-3 Dr.R.Kantharaju Orthopaedic surgeon has deposed that the Petitioner has sustained injuries in a RTA and he has not treated and Petitioner has sustained head injury with PTRA,
Fracture of 1st and 2nd rib with hydropneumothorax with collapse of underline lung parenchyma on a left side.

Compression fracture D6,D7 with fracture of spinous process of C7 , D4, D6 vertebra,
fracture of laminae of D5 and D6 vertebra, fracture of left foot 5th metatarsal left foot.
He was admitted at Victoria Hospital for treatment of loss of skin in left frontal region on 11-1-2023 and operated rotational flap with STSG.
He was discharged on 19-1- 2023.
he has under follow up treatment.
He found that Petitioner complains of difficulty to pick up of object while standing due to Shashikumar M.K vs Vedamurthy on 10 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/14556699/
5 upper back pain, headache on and off, squat on Indian toilet due to to back pain.

On examination he has assessed the total disability due to spinal and scalp injury 25% for whole body and compression of more than 50% involving single vertebra or more with involvement of posterior elements, healed,
no neurological manifestations, persistent paid, fusion, indicated 20% for whole body and disability due to ugly looking scar on left frontal region 5% whole body.
20. PW-3 in his cross-examination has stated that he has not treated the Petitioner.
He has stated that the fracture is united but it has been compressed.
denied that the disability may have chances to reduce in future.
He also denied the suggestion that the petitioner can do his work without any assistant.
It is pertinent to note that PW3 has assessed only physical disability and not functional disability.

Therefore, considering that the grievous injuries is on the head and spinal, considering the difficulties and evidence of PW-3 and also by considering the age of the Petitioner, the functional disability is assessed at 12%.
21. In the petition the age of the petitioner is mentioned as 28 years and in the wound certificate and other medical record it was mentioned age of the petitioner as 28 and 29 years.

Wherein Ex.P.9 Aadhar card shows that he was born on 23/12/1994, the same is considered as age of the deceased as on the date of accident as 29 years and the multiplier applicable to the case on hand is 17.
22.
The age of the petitioner is 29 years as on the date of accident.
Due to the accident he has sustained grievous injuries.
He was admitted in Victoria hospital at Benagaluru.
He has stated that at the time of accident, he was a Carpenter and was earning Rs.20,000/-P.M.
Due to the accidental injuries, he is unable to do his work and is unable to do his work as earlier and suffering huge loss of income.
However, the petitioner has not produced any documents to substantiate his income.
In the absence of material with regard to source of income, the tribunal has to be considered the national income chart of the Lok Adalath.
23. On perusal of the record, it appears that the age of the petitioner as on date of the alleged accident was about 29 years.
The alleged accident has taken place in the year 2023, the notional income of the injured could be assessed at Rs 16,000/- Per Month.

Thus this tribunal is of the opinion that the petitioner who sustained the injuries is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
24. Loss of future income on account of permanent disability: Looking into the nature of injuries
, it definitely affects the working capacity of any person.

As the Petitioner is a carpenter, considering nature of injury and doctor's evidence the total functional disability of the Petitioner is considered at 12%.
25.
The petitioner was aged about 29 years as on date of alleged accident and the multiplier applicable to the petitioner as per decision laid down by Hon'ble Apex court in Sarla Verma's case is at 17.
the national income taken as Rs 16,000 x 12 x 17 x 12/100= Rs.3,91,680/- towards loss of future income.

Shashikumar M.K vs Vedamurthy on 10 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/14556699/
6 26.
Pain and sufferings:

So far as the compensation under non-pecuniary damages are concerned,
considering the fact that the Petitioner has sustained head injuries and was inpatient for a period of 12 days which caused him to immeasurable mental agony and pain, I am of the opinion that an amount of .30,000/- would be just and fair compensation under the head pain and sufferings.
27. Loss of amenities of life:
For loss of amenities of life undoubtedly Petitioner is sure to suffer in his day today activities and face hardships.
Hence, Petitioner is awarded .25,000/- under loss of amenities of life.
28. Medical expenses:
Under the pecuniary damages, expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization and medicines, the Petitioner has produced medical bills at Ex.P.14 amounting to 88,690/-.
The Respondent has not seriously disputed the medical bills.
Hence, Petitioner is awarded compensation of 88,690/- towards Medical Expenses.
29. Conveyance, food, nourishment and attendant charges:

Ex.P.10-Discharge summary shows that Petitioner was treated as an inpatient at Digvijay Hospital from 08-01-2023 to 10-01-2023 and Ex.P.11 - discharge summary shows that again he was admitted at Victoria Hospital as an inpatient from 11- 01-2023 to 19-01-2023 i.e, for a period of 12 days .
Therefore, it is just and reasonable to award compensation of .20,000/- under the head of conveyance, food, nourishment and attendant charges.
30. Disfiguration and loss of marriage prospects:
Ex.P.13 are the photographs.
According to these photographs the petitioner has suffered disfiguration on left frontal region and he has lost marriage prospects and he might not get bride.
Considering these two aspects, Petitioner is awarded compensation of .20,000/- towards loss of marriage prospects and disfiguration.
31. Loss of earning during laid up period:

With regard to loss of earnings during treatment,
considering 12 days admission in the hospital as inpatient and around 3 months for rest is considered and loss of earnings during treatment is calculated for 3 months.

As the monthly income of the Petitioner is already considered as .16,000/- per month, loss of earning during laid up period would be .16,000 x 3 = 48,000/-.
32.

Thus the compensation awarded under the various heads are as under:

No .
1. Loss of future earnings . 3,91,680/-
2. Pain and Sufferings . 30,000/-

3. Loss of amenities . 25,000/-
4. Medical expenses . 88,690/-
5. Conveyance, Food, . 20,000/-
 Nourishment & Attendant  charges 6. Loss of marriage prospects and . 20,000/-

sentences.text: Liability: Respondent No.2 being the owner and the Respondent No.1 being the insurer of the offending lorry are jointly and severally liable to pay the above compensation.
However, Respondent No.2 is liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner with interest at 6% p.a.
With these observation I answer Issue No.3 partly in the affirmative.
34. ISSUE NO.4 :

In view of the above discussion, reasons stated and findings given to above Issues,
I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER Claim Petition filed under Sec.166 of M.V.Act is allowed in part with cost.
Petitioner is awarded compensation of Rs.6,23,370/- together with interest @ 6%
p.a. from the date of petition till the date of deposit with the Tribunal.
Respondent No.2 shall pay the aforesaid amount within two months from the date of this order.

After deposit of the compensation amount, 25% shall be kept in FD in the name of Petitioner in any nationalized or scheduled bank of his choice for a period of 2 years and remaining 75% with entire interest shall be disbursed to him through E-payment on proper identification.
Advocate's fee is fixed at .1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
